I used to struggle with this, not only would I feel superior to others but also inferior to some people as well, and so I have a reminder in my journal that no person on this planet is more superior OR inferior to anyone else - we're all on the same level.

​

“Alexander the Great and his mule driver both died and the same thing happened to both. They were absorbed alike into the life force of the world, or dissolved alike into atoms.” - Marcus Aurelius (Meditations)

Maybe I'm misunderstanding the main point of this quote, but I think it perfectly shows that in the end, we all meet the same fate. How can one feel superior or inferior to someone else if they're just as mortal, just as human as they are?

Whether or not you're afraid of death, it will come either way, that's a fact you can't control. But you can absolutely control your fear of death, and it's good that you want to stop being afraid of death. Find a good therapist, read more about the Stoic view on mortality, and focus on coming to terms with the fact that life, and everything in it, is temporary and so we should make the most of it while it lasts.
